title: Before the clock
narrative: Attention starts as a quality fix, not an efficiency trick. The RNN encoder–decoder squeezed a whole sentence into one vector and BLEU collapsed past ~30 words; Bahdanau's soft alignment (2014) let the decoder look back at every source state, Luong (2015) showed a plain dot product does the job with zero extra parameters, and learned absolute positions (MemN2N 2015, ConvS2S May 2017) gave order-blind layers a sense of place. Nobody was counting FLOPs yet — the bill had not arrived.

title: Wants exactness
wanted: parallel training + quality; pay O(n²) gladly
narrative: The Transformer throws the recurrence away and pays O(n²·d) per layer on purpose: every position sees every other in one hop, everything is a batched matmul, and the base model trains in 12 hours on 8 P100s. Positions are a footnote — the paper reports learned and sinusoidal as 'nearly identical' and picks sinusoids only in the hope of extrapolating. Shaw et al. (2018) add relative offsets for quality. Exact, dense, expensive — and nobody minds, because contexts are 512 tokens.

title: The bill arrives — wants compute back
narrative: Contexts grow past 1K and the quadratic term is suddenly the whole cost. The first efficiency wave tries every escape at once: recurrence for length (Transformer-XL), hand-designed sparsity (Sparse Transformer, Longformer, BigBird), content-routed sparsity (Reformer, Routing), keep-only-the-top-k, low rank (Linformer), and kernels that make attention linear (Katharopoulos, Performer). One paper — Shazeer's MQA — notices a different bill entirely: at decode time you re-read the whole KV cache for every token, and that is memory bandwidth, not FLOPs. Almost none of the approximations ship in language models (GPT-3 takes the banded-sparse pattern); dense matmul on GPUs keeps winning on quality per dollar. The lesson the field learns: sparsity that the hardware cannot exploit is not a saving.

title: Positions become the lever
wanted: relative position for free; a promise of extrapolation
narrative: With the compute question parked, attention's *other* problem gets attacked: absolute positions cap the model at its training length. RoPE (Mar/Apr 2021) rotates queries and keys so the dot product depends only on the offset — no parameters, KV-cache friendly. ALiBi (Aug 2021) throws positions away and just penalises distance linearly, and trains short to test long. Quietly, in February, Schlag/Irie/Schmidhuber show linear transformers are fast-weight programmers and fix their overwrite problem with the delta rule — the seed of DeltaNet, ignored for three years.

title: Exact got cheap
narrative: FlashAttention (May 2022) changes nothing about the maths and everything about the bill: tile the computation so the n×n matrix never touches HBM, and exact attention becomes 2–4× faster and linear in memory. Overnight the 2020 approximations lose their reason to exist at ordinary lengths — why accept a quality hit for a speedup a kernel gives you for free? The field re-learns that a systems change can beat an algorithmic one. Meanwhile Haviv et al. show a decoder learns position with no positional encoding at all, a hint that will matter in 2025.

title: Wants length
wanted: context as the product; stretch what you have
narrative: The ChatGPT year: context length is suddenly a headline feature and everyone owns a RoPE model trained at 2–4K. GQA (May) squeezes the KV cache without MQA's quality hit; vLLM's PagedAttention (June) makes KV memory *the* number serving engineers watch. Then, in ten days of June, three ways to stretch RoPE without retraining appear — kaiokendev's interpolation blog, Meta's PI paper, and bloc97's NTK-aware post on Reddit, followed a day later by Dynamic NTK — and YaRN (Aug) unifies them. Code Llama simply raises the base frequency. StreamingLLM (Sep) explains why the first tokens must never be evicted (attention sinks); Mistral 7B ships a 4K sliding window in a mainstream model; Ring Attention shards attention across devices. And the linear thread wakes up for length: RWKV, RetNet, GLA, Mamba.

title: Wants memory back
wanted: the KV cache is the constraint at 128K+
narrative: At 128K tokens the KV cache, not the FLOPs, decides how many users a GPU can serve. DeepSeek-V2's MLA (May) compresses keys and values into a small latent and caches only that — a 57× reduction with no quality loss. The recurrent thread becomes competitive: Mamba-2 shows SSMs and linear attention are the same object, DeltaNet gets a parallel training algorithm, and Gated DeltaNet (Dec) combines gating with the delta rule. Gemma 2 interleaves local and global layers so most of the cache is bounded. Length recipes go mainstream (Llama 3.1's 128K, LongRoPE, Dual Chunk), and eviction/selection schemes (H2O, SnapKV, Quest, DuoAttention) trade recall for memory.

title: Hybrids — memory back again, sparsity that trains
wanted: few exact layers, cheap everything else
narrative: The two efficiency threads converge on the same shape. Linear/recurrent layers carry most of the depth with a few exact attention layers for recall — MiniMax-01 (Jan), Qwen3-Next's 3:1 Gated DeltaNet (Sep), Kimi Linear (Oct). Positions get out of the way: Cohere, Llama 4 and SWAN interleave NoPE global layers with RoPE local ones. Sparsity finally becomes *trainable and hardware-aligned* — NSA's compress/select/window branches (Feb), MoBA, and DeepSeek's DSA in V3.2 (Sep) — so the exact layers themselves read only a few thousand of a million tokens. gpt-oss ships learned attention sinks and 128-token banded layers; Gemma 3 goes 5:1 local:global. Every one of these is the same sentence: pay full price for a small part of the model, and make the rest nearly free.

title: Now — compress, then select; the hybrids become defaults
wanted: 1M as the default: compressed KV, selected by an index; positions as a training aid
narrative: DroPE (Sakana, Dec 2025) treats RoPE as scaffolding: train with it, then drop it and briefly recalibrate, and the model extends its context zero-shot — the 2021 lever, removed. Then 2026 makes the timeline's prediction concrete. The hybrids become defaults: Qwen3.5 (Feb) runs 45 of 60 layers on Gated DeltaNet, Olmo Hybrid, Ling-2.5 and Kimi K3 (Jul, 69 KDA + 24 gated MLA at 2.8T) follow, and HALO shows a dense model can be converted into one for ~2B tokens. Sparse selection crosses lab lines: GLM-5 (Feb) adopts DSA and GLM-5.2 shares one indexer across four layers; MiniMax — which had abandoned its linear hybrid in M2 — comes back with block-sparse MSA in M3 (Jun). DeepSeek-V4 (Apr) ships Compressed Sparse Attention: compress every m tokens into one KV entry, let the lightning indexer pick the top-k *compressed* entries, keep a small window — interleaved with Heavily Compressed Attention, for 27% of V3.2's FLOPs and 10% of its KV at 1M. Gemma 4 (Apr) strips the global layers further (unified K/V, cross-layer sharing, p-RoPE). The delta rule gets its 2026 knob (Gated DeltaNet-2), the SSM thread its 2026 step (Mamba-3), and attention itself turns sideways (Attention Residuals, over depth). The exact layers no longer read tokens; they read a few compressed entries chosen by an index — and most layers are not attention at all.
